steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine beef, bread crumbs, onion, eggs, salt, and pepper in a large bowl; mix well. Pat out meat mixture into a 14x18-inch rectangle on a piece of wax paper.

Spread cheese over meat, leaving a 3/4 inch border along the edges. Roll up jelly-roll fashion to enclose the filling and form a pinwheel loaf. Press meat in on both ends to enclose cheese. Place meatloaf in a 10x15-inch baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until cooked through, about 1 hour. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of meatloaf should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Cheeseburger Meatloaf
raw_recipe.description: This cheeseburger meatloaf is stuffed with Cheddar cheese inside, but it can be substituted with other ingredients, like sautéed onions and mushrooms.

review.reviewBody:
I did my first loaf after reading all the reviews and my husband loves it. I'd like to suggest letting the loaf sit for 15 minutes before cutting, this will prevent oozing of the cheese. 
When I made it the second time, I dicovered a way to simplify the rolling process and had great success.
I divided my meat mixture into 3 batches and cheese into 2 batches (like a lasagne). Fill the bottom of a 9x13 dish with the 1st batch, then sprinkle cheese on top, avoiding the edges.
I then pat the 2nd batch on top, taking a little care to seal the edges with a spatula. Cheese on top of that.
Finally, the 3rd batch of meat on top of that, sealing the edges again.
I then sprinkled ketchup and mustard overall. It came out tasting the same as the recipe indicated, but saves much time and effort.

This is a great recipe! I only gave it 4 stars because I found the "jelly-roll" effect to be more trouble than it was worth. Instead, I just half the meat mixture and make a channel for the cheese down the center and then top with the remaining meat mixture. It is much more simple and it isn't as messy! Tastes fantastic as is or is easy to jazz up too!

Delicious! Here are a few of my suggestions - to avoid the grease problem - use super lean beef - I used 95% lean, it wasn't greasy at all... also, I used mozzarella in the middle (part-skim). It was perfect! And, for those of you watching calories/fat, it's pretty friendly, only 3 WW points per slice!
This recipe is awesome!! I just made for the 2nd time. only I added 1 cup of bacon bits and DOUBLED the cheese!! Bacon Double cheese burger meatloaf. with BBQ sauce over the top!

Delicious. I took advice from another reviewer and flattened meat into rectangle. Then cut it in half and spread the shredded cheese on one half, and placed other half on top. I did omit all salt since cheese is salty. Because it "looked" rather bland, I mixed 1/3 cup catsup with two TBS of Worcestershire Sauce and spread on top of meat the last 15 minutes of cooking. (I also poured the excess grease off the meat before putting sauce on top). The recipe was easy to make and was delicious.,

I’ve noticed some people struggling with rolling into a jelly roll. Line a shallow baking (cookie) sheet with parchment, press meat mixture firmly and evenly on parchment. Spread shredded cheese, I also added 1/4 cup dill relish at this stage. Using parchment paper, start rolling from narrow end. Smoothing as you roll. Then enjoy this tasty meatloaf variation.

Yummy! I made a half recipe and checked it at 50 min. It was way over 160degF. So, if I made this small version again, I'd check it a lot earlier. For the half amount, I used an 8x4 loaf pan sprayed with cooking spray, placing half the meat, then a layer of Mexican blend cheese (a little less than specified and leaving room at the edges) and then the rest of the meat. I topped it with a glaze of ketchup, brown sugar and apple cider vinegar. I also added a little Worcestershire sauce and garlic and onion powders to the meat. Thanks Douglas....very good recipe!
Amazing, I altered it by stuffing with mushrooms and Italian cheese blend. I pressed it out on parchment paper and refrigerated it, to help it roll easier.

It was a decent starter recipe. 
I sauteed 1 onion and 2 tablespoons of minced garlic. I added 1/2 tsp garlic power, 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper, 1 teas. dried parsley, 1 tabl. ketchup, and 1 tabl. of A1 sauce. It was marvelous.

We loved this!
I added a bacon weave lattice and BBQ sauce on top, but followed the actual loaf recipe exactly.
Definitely going in the dinner rotation here!

I didn't have any trouble rolling it.
Patted it out on sprayed parchment paper, and used the paper to aid in rolling. Left it rolled tightly, and refrigerated for 1 hour before baking.

Delicious and easy! Wanted bacon cheeseburger so I added 1/2 cup of real bacon bits to the cheese and used saltines instead of bread. Made it the night before and used the layering method of assembly in a loaf pan. Refrigerate overnight and turn out onto a roasting pan before baking. AB does this to eliminate the dreaded soggy bottom. Topped with ketchup, mustard and brown sugar glaze. served with fried dill pickle chips, French fries and a garden salad with 1000 island for the full burger effect.

Rainy day = MEATLOAF!! Made this before.. very good! This time Ive added garlic parmesan bread crumbs. Wish me luck!! Curious tho.. what cheese does everyone use? I've done cheddar, sharp, tonight its Colby jack

I didn't do the jelly roll thing. I halved the recipe with only one pound of meat. I'm only cooking for two, and we're not crazy about leftovers. I just layered half the meat mixture, then the cheese, then the other half of the meat on top. I also used a loaf pan because of the small amount of ingredients. I added a ketchup/mustard/brown sugar mix on top. Deelish!!
Next time I will use less onions

It was all amazing. I gave 4 stars bc the cook time was off by about 45 minutes. Took 1:45 minutes to reach the internal temp. But it was fantastic. Sides were long ready though bc the cook time was so far off. Will cook again. Probably a lot of times. Now I know to wait longer to prep the sides.
Followed exactly, perfectly done, and very good
Sounds weird,but Kinda good, I like Weird stuff some anyway..
